definition_en: to examine two or more things to see how they are alike or different, or to say that one thing is like another
core_image: 把两只手伸到眼前，左右反复端详
scene: 买鞋的姑娘把两只鞋翻过来看鞋底和走线。She compared the two pairs before choosing.
sceneCN: 这里 compare 指「比较；对比」（第 1 个义项：查看异同）；句意是她在挑选之前把两双鞋比了比。

senses.title: To look for differences
senses.definition: to examine two things to see how they are alike or different
senses.definitionCN: 查看两样事物有何相同与不同
senses.example: Compare the two maps and mark the changes.
senses.exampleCN: 比较这两张地图，标出变化。
senses.why: The core act is setting two things on the same footing to judge them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心动作是把两物放在同一基准上判断。

senses.title: To say one thing is like another
senses.definition: to describe one thing as being like another
senses.definitionCN: 把一物描述成与另一物相似
senses.example: The poet compares the moon to a silver coin.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人把月亮比作一枚银币。
senses.why: Once things are side by side, the mind easily turns one into a picture of the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物一旦并置，人就容易把一物想象成另一物的样子。

senses.title: To be worth matching
senses.definition: to be good enough to be mentioned beside another
senses.definitionCN: 好到可以与另一者并列提及
senses.example: No singer can compare with her.
senses.exampleCN: 没有歌手能和她相比。
senses.why: Comparison can end in a verdict that two things are not equal.
senses.whyCN: 比较可以得出两者并不对等的结论。

intro.en: Compare comes from Latin comparare, to bring two things together as equals, from com, together, and par, equal.
intro.cn: compare 来自拉丁语 comparare，意为把两样东西作为同等者带到一起，由 com（一起）与 par（相等）构成。

items.en: Par meant equal, level, of the same standing.
items.cn: par 表示相等、齐平、地位相同。

items.en: Comparare meant to place two things side by side.
items.cn: comparare 意为把两样东西并排放置。

items.en: Old French comparer kept the plain everyday sense.
items.cn: 古法语 comparer 保留了朴素的日常含义。

items.en: English compare first meant to match one thing against another.
items.cn: 英语 compare 最初指拿一物去对照另一物。

items.en: It gained the softer sense of likening one thing to another.
items.cn: 后来它又添了把一物比作另一物的柔和含义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short verbs that differ from compare by one or two letters, and the meaning group names other verbs of matching and setting against.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compare 只差一两个字母的短动词，近义组列出其他表示对照与比配的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two hands held up to the eye, then move to likening and to being worth a place beside another.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从把两样东西举到眼前开始，再走到比作以及值得与之一比。

normal.en: Com- is together and par is equal, so compare means to weigh two things as equals.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，par 是相等，compare 就是把两样东西当同等者来称。

normal.en: Compare with looks at difference; compare to makes a picture.
normal.cn: compare with 看差异，compare to 造比喻。

normal.en: Shop around and compare prices before you pay.
normal.cn: 付钱之前多走几家，比一比价格。

normal.en: Two friends compare notes after a test.
normal.cn: 考完试，两个朋友交换一下看法。

normal.en: Beyond compare means nothing can stand beside it.
normal.cn: beyond compare 指没有东西能与它相比。

abstract.en: Picture two apples held up one in each hand.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手各举一个苹果。

abstract.en: Picture a poet pointing at the moon and then at a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象诗人先指月亮，再指一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a list of prices with two columns side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价目表，两列数字并排。

examples.en: Compare the two answers before you decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前先比较这两个答案。

examples.en: He compared her smile to morning light.
examples.cn: 他把她的微笑比作晨光。

examples.en: Few cities can compare with Paris for food.
examples.cn: 论美食，很少有城市能与巴黎相比。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compare 记成 com（一起）加 pare（看作相等）：把两样东西放在一起看成同等，就是比较。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare，com- 表示一起，par 表示相等，本义是把事物作为同等者并列审视，后引申为比较与比作。

sensesIntro.en: From checking two things, to likening one to another, and finally to being worthy of comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 从查考两样东西，到把一物比作另一物，最后到值得与之相比。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands held at eye level, turning objects over side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：把两只手伸到眼前，左右反复端详两样东西。

branches.en: The plain act of checking two things is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 查看两样东西这个朴素动作是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Likening grows out of the same side-by-side picture.
branches.cn: 比作正是从同一个并置的画面里长出来的。

branches.en: A comparison can also end with one side clearly ahead.
branches.cn: 比较也可以以一方明显领先收尾。

branches.en: Both put two things in one frame, one to judge, one to picture.
branches.cn: 两者都把两物放进同一画框，一个为判断，一个为想象。

branches.en: You cannot say who is better without first comparing.
branches.cn: 不先比较，就说不出谁更好。

intro.en: Compare is a free base from Latin comparare; endings mark its tense and its relatives.
intro.cn: compare 是来自拉丁语 comparare 的自由词基，词尾变化标记时态，也生成同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin par, equal, is the small root that holds the family together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 par（相等）是把这个词族系在一起的小词根。

sceneCN: 这里 comparison 指「比较」（第 1 个义项：把事物放在一起对照）；句意是这番比较让选择容易多了。

senses.title: The act of comparing
senses.definition: the act of examining two or more things to see how they differ
senses.definitionCN: 检查两样或更多事物以看出差别的行为
senses.example: A comparison of the two reports shows one clear error.
senses.exampleCN: 对比两份报告，能看出一个明显错误。
senses.why: The noun names the whole act, from first look to final judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指整个过程，从最初一看直到最后判断。

senses.title: A stated likeness
senses.definition: a statement that one thing is like another
senses.definitionCN: 说一物像另一物的表述
senses.example: The poem uses a comparison between life and a journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗把人生比作一段旅程。
senses.why: When two things are held together long enough, one becomes an image of the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物并置久了，一物就成了另一物的形象。

senses.title: A basis for judging
senses.definition: the way two things can be measured against each other
senses.definitionCN: 两物可以相互衡量的方式
senses.example: There is no comparison between the two teams this season.
senses.exampleCN: 本赛季这两支队伍没法相提并论。
senses.why: The word also names the standard itself, the ground on which a judgement is made.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指标准本身，即作出判断所依据的基准。

intro.en: Comparison comes from Latin comparatio, the noun of comparare, to set things side by side.
intro.cn: comparison 来自拉丁语 comparatio，是 comparare（把事物并排放置）的名词形式。

items.en: Comparare meant to weigh two things against each other.
items.cn: comparare 意为让两样东西相互衡量。

items.en: Comparatio named the act and the result of that weighing.
items.cn: comparatio 指这种衡量的动作与结果。

items.en: Old French comparaison carried the noun into common use.
items.cn: 古法语 comparaison 把这个名词带进日常使用。

items.en: English comparison first meant a setting of two things together.
items.cn: 英语 comparison 最初指把两样东西放在一起。

items.en: It grew to cover figures of speech and fair grounds for judging.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到修辞上的比喻与公平判断的依据。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the shape of comparison, and the meaning group names other ways of contrasting or drawing a parallel.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comparison 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示对照或类比的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two maps on one table, then move to a spoken likeness and to the ground of a fair judgement.

normal.en: Comparison is the noun of compare: the act turned into a thing.

sensesIntro.en: From the act of comparing, to a stated likeness, and finally to the standard behind a judgement.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two maps spread open, one finger moving between the same two points.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开两张地图，手指在相同的位置来回移动。

branches.en: The act itself is the plainest sense of the noun.

branches.en: A likeness spoken aloud is a comparison made of words.
branches.cn: 说出口的相似，就是用语言做成的比较。

branches.en: Every judgement needs a standard to compare against.
branches.cn: 每个判断都需要一个可对照的标准。

branches.en: Both put two things in one frame for the mind to hold.
branches.cn: 两者都把两物放进同一画框，好让心里握住。

branches.en: The act and its standard are two halves of one judgement.
branches.cn: 比较的动作与它的标准，是同一个判断的两半。

intro.en: Comparison is built on the verb compare with the noun ending -ison.

sceneCN: 这里 compete 指「竞争」（第 1 个义项：争取胜过他人）；句意是小店很难与大型连锁店竞争。

senses.title: To strive against others
senses.definition: to try hard to gain something that others also want
senses.definitionCN: 努力争取别人也想要的东西

senses.exampleCN: 五家公司争夺同一份合同。

senses.title: To take part in a contest

senses.whyCN: 从努力争取，这个词收窄到有规则与终点的正式比赛。

intro.en: Compete comes from Latin competere, to seek something together, from com, together, and petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 来自拉丁语 competere，意为一起追求某物，由 com（一起）与 petere（追求）构成。

items.en: Petere meant to seek, to aim at or to ask for.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求、瞄准或请求。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same thing as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一样东西。

items.en: It also meant to be fit for a task or an office.
items.cn: 它也指适合某项任务或职位。

items.en: Old French competir narrowed it to rivalry.
items.cn: 古法语 competir 把词义收窄到争胜。

items.en: English compete covered both trade rivals and sports.
items.cn: 英语 compete 同时覆盖商业对手与体育竞技。

note.en: The look-alike group holds verbs one letter away from compete, and the meaning group ranks the verbs of rivalry.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compete 只差一个字母的动词，近义组排出表示争胜的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one prize and many hands, then move to shops that cut prices and to races with rules.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个奖赏与许多只手开始，再走到压价的小店与有规则的赛跑。

normal.en: Com- is together and pete means seek, so compete is to seek the same thing together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pete 是寻求，compete 就是一起去求同一样东西。

normal.en: Compete with a rival, compete for a prize, compete in a race.
normal.cn: 与对手 compete with，为奖品 compete for，在赛场上 compete in。

normal.en: The noun is competition, the person is a competitor.
normal.cn: 名词是 competition，人就是 competitor。

normal.en: Competitive prices keep a small shop alive.
normal.cn: 有竞争力的价格让小店的活路得以延续。

normal.en: You cannot compete if you never enter.
normal.cn: 不进场，就谈不上竞争。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching for one last ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手同时伸向最后一张票。

abstract.en: Picture two shops posting new prices in one morning.
abstract.cn: 想象两家店在同一个早上挂出新价签。

abstract.en: Picture five swimmers bent on the blocks, waiting for the whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象五名泳者伏在出发台上，等着哨声。

examples.en: Small firms must compete on quality.
examples.cn: 小公司必须在质量上竞争。

examples.en: He competed against runners from ten countries.
examples.cn: 他与来自十个国家的跑者同场竞技。

examples.en: Two cities competed for the new factory.
examples.cn: 两座城市争夺这家新工厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compete 记成 com（一起）加 pete（寻求）：大家一起伸手去求同一个东西，就是竞争。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，com- 表示一起，petere 表示追求，本义是一起追求同一个目标，后引申为竞争与参赛。

sensesIntro.en: From striving for one prize, to entering a contest with rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 从为同一个奖赏而努力，到参加有规则的比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners side by side on one track, driving toward the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两名跑者在同一条跑道上并排冲向终点。

branches.en: Striving for a shared goal is the root sense.
branches.cn: 为共同目标而努力，是这个词的词根义。

branches.en: A contest is the same striving with rules added.
branches.cn: 比赛就是同样的争胜加上了规则。

branches.en: Shops and runners both want to finish first.
branches.cn: 商店与跑者都想第一个到达。

branches.en: The word needs a rival; nobody competes alone.
branches.cn: 这个词需要一个对手；没有人独自竞争。

branches.en: To compete in an event is to accept its rules.
branches.cn: 参加一项比赛，就是接受它的规则。

intro.en: Compete is built on Latin com, together, plus petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 petere（追求）构成。

latinIntro.en: The seeking base pet- also appears in appetite and petition.
latinIntro.cn: 表示追求的词基 pet- 也出现在 appetite 与 petition 里。

items.example: She competes in long-distance races.
items.exampleCN: 她参加长跑比赛。

items.example: The team competed in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍在三座城市参赛。

items.example: The two are competing for the same buyers.
items.exampleCN: 两家在争夺同一批买家。

items.example: The competition starts at nine.
items.exampleCN: 比赛九点开始。

items.example: She entered three competitions.
items.exampleCN: 她参加了三场比赛。

items.example: The market is very competitive.
items.exampleCN: 市场竞争非常激烈。

items.meaning: a person or firm you compete with
items.example: Our main competitor cut its prices.
items.exampleCN: 我们的主要对手降价了。

items.example: Training raises the team's competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 训练提高了队伍的竞争力。

definition_en: an event in which people try to win, or the rivalry between people or firms who want the same thing
core_image: 几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水
scene: 报名表贴出三天，走廊里已经挤满了准备参赛的学生。The competition attracted students from twenty schools.
sceneCN: 这里 competition 指「比赛」（第 1 个义项：争夺名次的活动）；句意是这场比赛吸引了二十所学校的学生。

senses.title: A contest
senses.definition: an event in which people try to win a prize
senses.definitionCN: 人们争夺奖项的活动
senses.example: She won the writing competition at school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校作文比赛中获奖。
senses.why: A fixed event with rules turns rivalry into something you can watch and score.
senses.whyCN: 有规则、有场地的活动，把争胜变成看得见、可评分的事。

senses.title: Rivalry between people or firms
senses.definition: the struggle between people or companies for the same aim
senses.definitionCN: 人或公司为同一目标而进行的争夺
senses.example: Price competition keeps the market healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 价格竞争让市场保持健康。
senses.why: The same striving continues without a referee, in shops and offices.
senses.whyCN: 同样的争胜在没有裁判的商店与办公室里继续。

senses.title: The rivals themselves
senses.definition: the people or firms you are trying to beat
senses.definitionCN: 你想要胜过的那些人或公司
senses.example: The competition has cut its prices again.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手又降价了。
senses.why: By a small shift, the contest comes to mean the other side in it.
senses.whyCN: 词义轻轻一转，比赛就指比赛里的对方。

intro.en: Competition comes from Latin competitio, the noun of competere, to seek the same thing together.
intro.cn: competition 来自拉丁语 competitio，是 competere（一起追求同一目标）的名词形式。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same prize as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一个奖赏。

items.en: Competitio named the shared striving itself.
items.cn: competitio 指这种共同的争求本身。

items.en: It also described a legal claim between two parties.
items.cn: 它也描述两方之间的法律争讼。

items.en: Old French competition narrowed to contests and trade.
items.cn: 古法语 competition 收窄到比赛与商业。

items.en: English competition covered sport, markets and rival firms.
items.cn: 英语 competition 覆盖体育、市场与对手公司。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other -tion nouns easily confused with competition, and the meaning group separates a contest, a rivalry and a match.
note.cn: 形近组收的是容易与 competition 混淆的其他名词，近义组分辨竞赛、对抗与一场比赛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with boats on one line, then move to the everyday struggle and to the rivals on the other side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从同一条起跑线上的船开始，再走到日常的争夺以及对面的对手。

normal.en: Competition is the noun behind compete: it names the whole scene.
normal.cn: competition 是 compete 背后的名词：它给整个场面命名。

normal.en: Enter a competition, win a competition, but feel competition in a market.
normal.cn: 可以说参加比赛、赢得比赛，也会在市场里感受到竞争。

normal.en: Fierce competition is the phrase shops use when prices fall.
normal.cn: 降价时商家会说竞争激烈，用的就是 fierce competition。

normal.en: The competition can also be the other team, not the event.
normal.cn: the competition 也可以指对方队伍，而不是那场活动。

normal.en: A competitor is one person; competition is the whole field.
normal.cn: competitor 是一个人，competition 是整个赛场。

abstract.en: Picture five oars hitting the water at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象五支桨在同一秒入水。

abstract.en: Picture two price boards changing in the same street.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条街上两块价目牌先后更换。

abstract.en: Picture a judge holding a list of names and a stopwatch.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判拿着名单和秒表。

examples.en: The design competition drew over a hundred entries.
examples.cn: 这次设计比赛收到一百多件作品。

examples.en: Fierce competition forced the shop to close.
examples.cn: 激烈的竞争迫使这家店关门。

examples.en: Our competition launched a cheaper model.
examples.cn: 我们的竞争对手推出了一款更便宜的型号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competition 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ition：一群人一起追同一个奖品，就是竞争与比赛。

root: 源自拉丁语 competitio，由 competere（一起追求）加名词后缀而来，本义是共同争求同一目标，后指比赛、竞争与对手。

sensesIntro.en: From a scored contest, to the everyday struggle, and finally to the rivals in it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从计分的比赛，到日常的争夺，最后到争夺中的对手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several boats pressed against one starting line, oars entering the water at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水。

branches.en: The scored event is the clearest sense of competition.
branches.cn: 计分的赛事是 competition 最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Without rules, the same striving becomes market rivalry.
branches.cn: 没有规则时，同样的争胜就成了市场竞争。

branches.en: The contest can stand for the other side in it.
branches.cn: 比赛可以代指比赛里的另一方。

branches.en: Both are one prize chased by many hands.
branches.cn: 两者都是许多只手去追同一个奖赏。

branches.en: In business the rivals are the competition.
branches.cn: 在生意里，对手就是 the competition。

intro.en: Competition joins the verb compete with the noun ending -ition.
intro.cn: competition 由动词 compete 加名词后缀 -ition 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin petere, to seek, is the small engine inside the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere（追求）是整个词族内部的小引擎。

items.exampleCN: 学校每年举办三场比赛。

items.exampleCN: 他们争夺同一批买家。

items.example: Our team competes every spring.
items.exampleCN: 我们队每年春天参赛。

items.example: She competed at national level.
items.exampleCN: 她参加过全国级比赛。

items.example: Two competing plans were on the table.
items.exampleCN: 桌上有两个相互竞争方案。

items.example: The firm stays competitive by cutting costs.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司靠削减成本保持竞争力。

items.example: Each competitor wore a number.
items.exampleCN: 每位参赛者都戴着一个号码。

items.example: The index measures economic competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 这个指数衡量经济竞争力。
